canonical_title: Duplicate/conflicting processing-intent detection belongs in the planning step itself, keyed on full validated content, not on path strings or on classification-output alone
summary: S5-F-04 found that two distinct closure-envelope files claiming the same mission_id plus closure_revision each produced their own separate eligible work item, because the reconciliation CLI only deduplicated identical file-path strings, not duplicate processing identity. The fix moved identity grouping into planReconciliation itself, keyed on mission_id::closure_revision, and compared group members by a full-content hash (not just the narrower fingerprint/classification-relevant fields) -- so a difference in a field the classifier never reads is still correctly detected as a material conflict, not silently ignored.

claims.text: The reconciliation CLI's path-string Set only removed identical file-path strings; it did not recognize that two different files could both legitimately claim the same mission_id plus closure_revision processing identity, so each independently produced its own ELIGIBLE_UNPROCESSED work item.

evidence.locator: Section 7, 'Finding': 'Two distinct valid envelope files claiming the same mission_id + closure_revision each produced their own ELIGIBLE_UNPROCESSED work item; the CLI's path-string Set only removes identical path strings, not duplicate processing identity.'

claims.text: The fix deliberately compares each identity group's members by a hash of the full validated envelope object rather than only the subset of fields the classification algorithm reads, because two envelopes could differ only in a field classification never consumes (such as accepted_scope) and still represent a materially different processing intent that must be treated as an unsafe conflict, not silently deduplicated.

evidence.locator: Section 7, 'Correction': 'comparing classification output alone would miss a material difference in a field classification does not itself read (e.g. accepted_scope). A group with one distinct hash classifies its single representative once; a group with more than one distinct hash emits zero work items and one safe, deterministic conflict entry.'

Section 7, 'Proof', third bullet: 'Two envelopes differing only in accepted_scope (a field classification does not consume) are still correctly detected as conflicting and produce zero work items, deterministically, across reversed replay -- directly validating that conflict detection compares full envelope content, not merely classification output.'

claims.text: Materially conflicting envelopes under the same identity produce zero work items plus a single safe conflict entry that names only the mission_id::closure_revision identity and never echoes raw envelope content such as the commit SHA -- a fail-closed outcome that also avoids leaking potentially sensitive disputed-content details into a diagnostic message.

evidence.locator: Section 7, 'Proof', second bullet: 'Two envelopes for the same mission/revision with a genuinely different pinned source_snapshot_ref/evidence produce zero work items and one conflict entry whose reason names the identity and contains "conflicting", with the commit SHA never echoed.'

conditions: Applies to any system that plans or schedules work from a set of discovered input files/records where more than one input could legitimately or accidentally claim the same logical processing identity.

Requires the identity key to be a stable, meaningful domain concept (here, mission_id::closure_revision), and requires comparing candidates for that identity by their full validated content, not merely by the narrower subset of fields any single downstream consumer happens to read.
anti_patterns: Deduplicating discovered work items by file path or filename alone, which only catches literally identical inputs and misses distinct files that represent the same underlying duplicate or conflicting processing intent.

Comparing candidate duplicates only by the fields a specific downstream algorithm consumes, which can silently miss a materially different input that happens to differ only in a field that algorithm ignores -- exactly the accepted_scope case this correction proved against.
